topSignals.title: Crusoe + Aalo Atomics announce first nuclear-AI factory partnership (July 30) — Crusoe hedges its Bloom SOFC portfolio with nuclear
topSignals.text: — Announced July 30, 2026, Crusoe Energy and Aalo Atomics formed a strategic partnership to build the world's first nuclear-powered AI data center. A Crusoe Spark modular data center will be deployed at Idaho National Laboratory (INL) in 2027, powered directly by Aalo's Pod reactor — a 50 MWe unit comprising five 10 MWe Aalo-1 microreactors plus a power-generating turbine. Full portfolio deployment of Aalo Pods across Crusoe's data center estate targeted by end of 2029. This is the most specific commercial nuclear-AI timeline announced to date, and comes from the same operator (Crusoe) already deploying Bloom SOFCs at the 1.8 GW Cheyenne campus — confirming that major AI compute operators see SOFCs as the near-term (2026-2028) bridge and nuclear as the long-run (2029+) option, not a replacement. Aalo's Aalo-X Critical Test Reactor achieved criticality at INL on July 4, 2026. GlobeNewswire | DCD | Power Magazine

topSignals.title: BE surges to $210.67 on August 2 — full recovery from post-earnings trough confirmed
topSignals.text: — Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE) traded at $210.67 on August 2 (+28.7% or +$46.92 from its recent close), completing the recovery from the $159.80 intraday low on July 31. Multiple analyst notes published post-July 28 Q2 earnings frame the sell-off as overdone: Seeking Alpha's "Bloom Energy: Strong Q2 2026 Suggests The Recent Sell-Off Went Too Far" is representative of the emerging consensus. 29 analyst average PT $273.51 (+29% upside from $210.67). All analyst PTs remain above current price; Q3 2026 is now the next earnings catalyst. Seeking Alpha | StockAnalysis | Yahoo Finance

topSignals.title: FERC RM26-4: abeyance deadline is tomorrow (August 3) — model trigger in 24 hours
topSignals.text: — All six RTOs/ISOs must submit full or partial abeyance requests by August 3, 2026 (45 days from the June 18 Show Cause Orders). ISO New England confirmed (August 1) it will file for 90-day abeyance. FERC has stated it will "heavily scrutinize" requests but will consider them; a granted abeyance runs to November 16. The outcome on August 3-4 determines whether the $5-20/MWh avoided-T-cost benefit for SOFC self-supply projects becomes a live LCOE input now (if denied, August 17 hard deadline) or is deferred to Q4 (if granted). Schedule LCOE model update for August 4. FERC RM26-4 | Day Pitney analysis | McGuireWoods

items.text: Elcogen: Quiet day. EFCF 2026 (Lucerne, June 30–July 3) proceedings remain under peer-review embargo — now exceeding 5 weeks since conference close. ELCO I Tallinn factory (360 MW/yr) continuing production and E3000 G2 deliveries. No new announcements. Status: watch elcogen.com for embargo lift.

Topsoe: Quiet day. Status unchanged: Herning SOEC factory hibernated pending commercial-scale H2 demand (strategy adjustment confirmed May 2026); CEO Elena Scaltritti since June 1, 2026. SOFC data-center pathway deferred to 2029+ per H2 market constraints. No new announcements August 2.

Topco + Bloom Energy: Taiwan's first on-site SOFC data center power system (first full appearance) — Topco Scientific and Bloom Energy installed Taiwan's first on-site SOFC low-carbon data center power system, reaching full capacity in June 2026. The 2.6 MW system is projected to generate approximately 21.6 million kWh annually, serving a Topco data center facility. This is the first confirmed SOFC data center deployment in Taiwan, marking the Asia-Pacific market entry for large-scale SOFC on-site DC power. Digitimes | Taiwan News

Topco + Bloom Energy Taiwan (2.6 MW, June 2026) — See Stack & Cell Technology above. Small scale relative to US hyperscaler deployments, but confirms Asia-Pacific SOFC DC deployment as active (not just pipeline). Digitimes identifies two emerging supply ecosystems: Bloom direct, and Ceres-licensed (Delta Electronics, Doosan, Weichai) targeting post-2027 commercial scale. Digitimes SOFC supply chain

Crusoe nuclear hedge — See Top Signal #1. Crusoe's simultaneous deployment of Bloom SOFCs (1.8 GW Cheyenne Phase 1) and Aalo nuclear (50 MWe INL demo 2027, portfolio target 2029) confirms the emerging two-tier strategy: SOFC for 2026-2028 baseload, nuclear as 2029+ scale option. Active SOFC pipeline unchanged: Oracle/Jupiter 2.45 GW (NM air permit hearing October 19), Crusoe/Cheyenne 900 MW Phase 1, FCEL/Fit Energy 380 MW (30 MW initial delivery H2 2026), Equinix >100 MW, Bloom/Brookfield $25B, Nebius 328 MW EaaS.

FERC RM26-4 — deadline August 3 (tomorrow) — See Top Signal #3. All six RTOs/ISOs (PJM, MISO, CAISO, ISO-NE, NYISO, SPP) face the abeyance filing deadline. ISO-NE confirmed August 1 it will file. No surprise outcomes expected; FERC has signaled it will grant abeyance for stakeholder process but will limit it to 90 days and disfavor extensions. If denied (low probability): August 17 hard deadline triggers immediate tariff reform. If granted (high probability): November 16 stakeholder filing deadline. Update LCOE model August 4. FERC RM26-4 docket | Baker Botts analysis
Quiet otherwise. NY moratorium (50 MW+ threshold), EU CADA (rating scheme still delayed), Germany EnEfG (PUE ≤1.2 / ERF ≥10% from July 2026): no changes.

Crusoe + Aalo Atomics nuclear demo (INL 2027) — See Top Signal #1. The 50 MWe Aalo Pod is the most technically specified nuclear-AI data center project to date. Portfolio-wide Crusoe deployment target: end of 2029. Competitive implication: nuclear becomes a credible option for AI compute from 2030, not 2035+ as some timelines assumed. SOFC's 90-day deployment advantage remains unchallenged through at least 2028. Data Center Frontier

Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists (July 2026): "Data centers powered by next-gen nuclear? Don't fall for Big Tech's PR hype" — Second major independent critical analysis this summer (after Carnegie Endowment June 2026). Key arguments: hyperscaler nuclear commitments are performative because grid-scale HALEU fuel supply chains don't exist, new-build timelines are 10+ years regardless of MOUs, and regulatory licensing remains multi-year. Reinforces the structural SOFC opportunity through 2029. Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists

Background: Microsoft Project Kilby (2.67 GW CCGT, Texas, first power 2028), DOE $17.5B AP1000 nuclear loans (10+ year horizon), Google Meitner Energy Center (wind/solar/battery + gas firming, Texas Panhandle) — covered June 27–28.

Bloom Energy (BE) — $210.67 on August 2 (+28.7% recovery from recent close). Continuing recovery from $159.80 intraday low (July 31) and July 30 close (~$163). All 29 analyst PTs remain above current price; consensus $273.51 (+29% implied upside). Seeking Alpha | Investing.com earnings call

FuelCell Energy (FCEL) — ~$23 range. UBS raised PT to $27 (timing: likely post-July 30 sympathy rally, upgrade from prior $22 Neutral). Prior analyst picture: B. Riley Buy $32, Jefferies Buy $24. Q2 FY2026: revenue $35.6M (−4.9% YoY), operating loss $77.9M. $225M equity offering (July 7-8). Q3 FY2026 earnings (October) is next catalyst. CNBC | MarketBeat
Ceres Power (LON: CWR) — Quiet. ~−40% from June peak; H1 2026 results (September) remain next catalyst. First royalties received confirms licensee manufacturing at commercial scale.

ACS Chemistry of Materials: "Operando Techniques for the Study of Solid Oxide Fuel Cells: A Review" (2026) — New comprehensive review of in-situ and operando measurement methodologies for SOFCs at operating temperatures ≥400°C. Covers XRD, X-ray tomography, spectroscopy, and impedance techniques applicable to degradation monitoring in commercial stack operation. Relevant for: (a) lifetime verification in field-deployed commercial systems, (b) chromium poisoning and LSCF cathode Sr-migration detection — the dominant degradation mechanisms identified in the Jülich 93,000-hour study. Not system-level, but methodologically useful for stack operators. ACS Chemistry of Materials

lcoe.text: BE $210.67 recovery: WACC revision signal — With BE above $200 on August 2 and market consensus forming around "sell-off overdone" ($273 avg PT), revise WACC sensitivity band downward: from 10.5–11% (Aug 1) to 10–10.5%. If BE holds above $200 through week end, further revise toward 9.5–10% (pre-earnings baseline). Bloom's cost of capital directly affects its EaaS $/MWh pricing — lower WACC = lower bundled power rate to customers.

FERC RM26-4 model trigger (August 4): If abeyance denied (low probability): activate $5–20/MWh avoided transmission cost as live LCOE input for PJM/MISO/CAISO/ISO-NE on-site SOFC scenarios. If granted (high probability): hold as placeholder; revisit November 16. No model change until FERC publishes its response to August 3 filings.

Crusoe nuclear hedge — SOFC LCOE competitive window: Crusoe's end-of-2029 Aalo Pod portfolio target implies nuclear does not displace SOFCs before 2030 even at the most accelerated commercial operator. Maintain SOFC as the sole available 24/7 baseload on-site option for AI data centers through 2028-2029. Do not introduce nuclear as a competitive scenario before 2030 in the LCOE model.

Taiwan SOFC deployment (Topco/Bloom 2.6 MW): No capex disclosure. At ~$1,600/kW implied ASP (directional, from Q2 earnings revenue/MW estimates), small deployments appear to carry a price premium vs. large US hyperscaler deals — consistent with the $2,944/kW AEP utility-scale benchmark. No LCOE model update warranted without actual capex figures.

Pending (carry-forward): Bloom 10-Q (within 45 days of July 28) for explicit shipped MW in Q2. EFCF proceedings embargo lift (Elcogen E3000 G2 efficiency at 650°C commercial scale). FERC RM26-4 August 3 outcome → model update August 4.
